title: A server will not start because something holds its port
prompt: The service in this folder (see README.md) will not start. Find out why, deal with it without editing server.py, start the service, save what GET /health returns into health.json, and stop the service again.
check:
python3 -c "import hashlib,json,os,socket,sys
h = json.load(open('health.json'))
assert h['status'] == 'ok'
assert h['secret'] == hashlib.sha1((os.environ['BENCH_SECRET'] + 'srv').encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
s = socket.socket(); s.settimeout(1)
port = int(open('port.txt').read())
sys.exit(1 if s.connect_ex(('127.0.0.1', port)) == 0 else 0)" && ! kill -0 "$(cat leftover.pid)" 2>/dev/null
setup:
python3 -c "import socket; s = socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])" > port.txt
printf "%s" "$(cat <<'EOF'
import socket, time
port = int(open("port.txt").read().strip())
s = socket.socket()
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
s.listen(1)
time.sleep(300)
EOF
)" > /tmp/navvied-leftover-$$.py
(python3 "/tmp/navvied-leftover-$$.py" >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > leftover.pid)
sleep 0.5
rm -f /tmp/navvied-leftover-$$.py
